links.note: Was 30774 (democracy is rule of the people), which is not what the item asks: it asks what separation of powers entails. This chapter's 18 concepts have no separation-of-powers, judiciary or rights concept - the same gap for which I left its short-answer twin unlinked. Cleared.
Was 30771 (what a government is for). 'What does separation of powers mean' is not a question about the functions of government; nothing in the closed set covers the three organs. Cleared.
Was 30771. The item asks what 'sovereign' means; no concept in this chapter's set covers sovereignty (the Constitution chapter has one, but that is a different closed set). Cleared.
Was 30771. The statement tested is whether fundamental rights are optional guidelines - a rights question, and no rights concept exists here. Cleared.
Was 30771. The statement is about the judiciary ensuring laws are followed; there is no judiciary concept in this set. Cleared.
Was 30771. The item asks which body checks new laws against the constitution - judicial review, which this set does not cover. Cleared.
Was 30771. A citizen's remedy when a fundamental right is violated is a rights-and-courts question with no concept in this set. Cleared.
Was 30771. 'Which organ protects fundamental rights' needs a judiciary concept, which this set lacks. Cleared.

Was 30780 (how a government is formed), which the item never touches: it asks why an independent judiciary is essential. No judiciary concept exists in this set, and its duplicate row is already unlinked for the same reason. Cleared.

Was 30772 (law and order, peace and security). The case study is about a prime minister restricting press freedom and the constitutional limits on that - rights and their protection, which this set does not cover. Cleared.
Was 30771 (the functions of government). The item matches national practices to types of government, which is 30779's axis - what gives each government its authority.
Was 30771. A ruler who seized power by force and is bound by no constitution is a dictatorship, classified by where authority comes from - 30779.
Was 30771. A general suspending the constitution after a coup is again the source-of-authority typology, 30779.
Was 30771. A ruler whose power is inherited and unlimited by a constitution is an absolute monarchy - 30780, which contrasts family succession with election.
Was 30771. The scenario (universal franchise, protected rights) is to be identified as a democracy, which is 30774 - the short definition the chapter uses as its test.
Was 30771. Regular free and fair elections with universal adult voting identify a democracy - 30774.
